model.name: Contact Point / Party Profile
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin that lets any governed party carry its contact channels together with the communication preferences, availability and routing inputs that describe how the party asks to be contacted, so that an agent can resolve an advisory contact plan without owning identity, message, delivery or legal-restriction semantics.
model.scope_statement: The combined WM-PER-010 covers three areas: (a) contact channel and endpoint descriptors attached to a party; (b) party-stated communication preferences, availability and routing inputs; (c) the governance of both, including provenance, versioning, precedence and the resolvable reference to an external communication-restriction registry. This delivery is one bounded split pass and populates structure.bundles, functions and evidence only for area (b) - preferences, routing and availability. The model is storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections, not semantics.
in_scope: Contact channel and endpoint descriptors attached to a party, including channel kind and capability metadata (combined-model area delivered by the channel split pass).
Party-stated communication preferences scoped by purpose class and usage context, including preferred and avoided channel modalities.
Availability inputs: time-zone reference, stated contact windows, effective intervals and temporary overrides.
Routing inputs: attempt order and fallback sequence, urgency tiers, escalation preference, delegation and alternate-contact designation.
Linguistic and accessibility accommodation directives that shape how a communication is rendered or conducted.

Governance of the mixin: statement provenance and authority, precedence and conflict rules, ruleset editions and the resolvable reference to an external communication-restriction registry (combined-model area delivered by the governance split pass).
out_of_scope: Party master identity, legal names, roles and life events, which belong to the parent party model WM-PER-001.
Legally governed communication restrictions, legal objections, consent evidence and legal-basis decisions, which belong to external restriction and consent models.
Message content, templates, campaigns, audience selection and personalisation logic.
Delivery, transmission, receipt and bounce events, retry logs and audit trails held by the sending and logging systems.
Endpoint reachability verification, address or number validation, portability lookups and directory services.
The calendar system of record: appointment booking, real free/busy computation over actual events and scheduling negotiation.
Enforcement: the act of sending, blocking, throttling or suppressing a communication, which is performed by the sending system under the external restriction record.
Jurisdiction-specific marketing, solicitation or quiet-hour rules as schema invariants; these are resolved externally and recorded here only as profile-conditional flags.

boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin attaches preference statements to a party reference. Party identity, naming, demographics and role history stay in the parent model; a preference statement never restates them.

The legal restriction record, its lifecycle, its evaluation engine and its enforcement remain external. This model carries only a resolvable reference plus a resolution status, and never creates, ends, weakens or reinterprets that record.
A party-stated preference is an operational request, not evidence of consent and not a legal-basis decision. Resolution output must never be read as a lawfulness determination.

This model records the party's stated contact windows as declared preference. Real free/busy computation over booked events, and scheduling negotiation, stay in the calendar system; RFC 7953 and RFC 8984 vocabulary are used as alignment only.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Contact channel and endpoint descriptor area of WM-PER-010
boundary_notes.distinction: Preference statements reference a channel kind or an endpoint handle. The endpoint address, its syntax, its verification state and its provider metadata belong to the channel area and are never duplicated in a preference statement.
A resolved contact plan is advisory input to a sender. Delivery events, attempt outcomes, retry state and audit trails are created, owned and retained by the sending and logging systems.

Only contact-scoped, functional accommodation directives are held here. A full functional-ability profile, assistive-technology inventory or any diagnostic information belongs to the accessibility or health model.

sources.title: RFC 9553: JSContact: A JSON Representation of Contact Data
sources.relevance: Normative source for contexts (private/work), the pref preference-order property (1-100, lower is more preferred), preferredLanguages with contexts and pref, phone feature values including textphone, and onlineServices preference ordering.

sources.title: RFC 6350: vCard Format Specification
sources.relevance: Normative rules for the PREF parameter (integer 1-100, absence means least preferred, value interpretable only relative to other instances of the same property), the LANG property for contact languages, the TZ property and its caution against fixed UTC offsets, and RELATED type values including agent and emergency.

sources.title: RFC 7953: Calendar Availability: A Standard Approach
sources.relevance: Normative model for recurring availability patterns: VAVAILABILITY with AVAILABLE subcomponents, BUSYTYPE defaulting uncovered time to BUSY-UNAVAILABLE, PRIORITY-based resolution of overlapping components with absence or 0 meaning lowest priority, and the equal-priority ordering BUSY > BUSY-UNAVAILABLE > BUSY-TENTATIVE.

sources.title: RFC 5646 (BCP 47): Tags for Identifying Languages
sources.version_or_date: RFC 5646 / BCP 47, September 2009, Best Current Practice
sources.relevance: Normative subtag structure for language, script, region, variant and private use, and the rule that a script subtag SHOULD be omitted when it adds no distinguishing value or when the registry record carries Suppress-Script.

sources.title: RFC 8984: JSCalendar: A JSON Representation of Calendar Data
sources.relevance: Normative pattern for timeZone, recurrenceRules, excludedRecurrenceRules and recurrenceOverrides as patch objects on individual occurrences, and freeBusyStatus - the basis for representing temporary overrides without rewriting a standing pattern.

sources.title: ContactPoint - Schema.org Type
sources.relevance: Vocabulary evidence that a party or organisation has multiple contact points differentiated by contactType (purpose), with availableLanguage bound to BCP 47, hoursAvailable, areaServed and contactOption.

sources.title: ContactPointOption - Schema.org Enumeration
sources.relevance: Shows the published accessibility-related contact option surface (HearingImpairedSupported, TollFree) and its narrowness relative to functional accommodation vocabularies, used to justify a capability-based rather than enumeration-based accommodation model.

sources.title: FHIR Release 5: Data Types (ContactPoint)
sources.relevance: Normative definition of ContactPoint with rank (positiveInt, lower values more preferred), period (time period when the contact point was or is in use) and the ContactPointUse value set home, work, temp, old, mobile, grounding preference ranking, validity intervals and temporary use.

sources.title: Time Zone Database
sources.relevance: Authoritative registry of Area/Location time-zone identifiers and their historical rules; updated periodically for political changes, which is why a stated window must cite both a zone identifier and the database release used to interpret it.

sources.title: vCard Elements Registries
sources.relevance: Normative registry of vCard properties, parameters (including PREF and LANGUAGE), value data types and property values (TEL types voice, fax, cell, video, pager, textphone, main-number; RELATED types including agent and emergency), plus the registration procedures that govern vendor-namespaced extensions.

sources.title: 1EdTech AccessForAll Personal Needs and Preferences Description for Digital Delivery Information Model
sources.version_or_date: Version 2.0 Final Release, 2010; aligned with ISO/IEC 24751
sources.relevance: Primary model for expressing accessibility needs functionally rather than diagnostically, organised as display, control and content adaptation preferences, with explicit support for multiple context-specific preference sets that a party switches between.

sources.title: Common Alerting Protocol Version 1.2
sources.relevance: Sector-neutral urgency vocabulary (Immediate, Expected, Future, Past, Unknown) with time-to-respond definitions, used only as an alignment candidate for urgency tiering; CAP alert dissemination semantics are not adopted.

bundles.name: Preference Declaration
bundles.description: What the party declares about how it wishes to be contacted: the scope a statement applies to, which modalities it prefers or asks to avoid, and the linguistic and accessibility directives that shape the communication itself.
bundles.rationale: Declaration is a coherent concern because every element is an assertion made by or for the party about desired treatment, independent of when contact happens or how a system resolves competing statements. Both vCard/JSContact and FHIR treat purpose context, preference ordering and language preference as properties of the contact description rather than of a transmission, which supports grouping them together and separating them from routing-time evaluation.

layers.name: Applicability Scope and Channel Disposition
layers.description: The scoping of a preference statement to a communication purpose and usage context, and the positive or negative disposition it expresses towards a channel modality.

findings.name: Preference applicability scope: purpose class, context and capacity
findings.description: The scope key that decides whether a preference statement applies to a given outbound or inbound interaction: the communication purpose class (for example service, administrative, scheduling, relationship or life-safety), the usage context (private or work), the party capacity in which the statement was made, and any profile-conditional flags that must be declared rather than assumed.

answer_data: treatment rule for unclassified requests
whether the most restrictive matching statement applies
reason code returned to the requester

questions.text: Which capacity does the statement cover when the same party acts as customer, employee and emergency contact?
answer_data: party capacity or role reference
scope key composition rule
cross-capacity leakage prohibition

questions.text: Which profile-conditional situations must be recorded explicitly instead of being inferred as defaults?
answer_data: profile condition flag such as workplace contact, minor, vulnerable person or life-safety

data_elements.name: Profile condition flag

findings.inline_only_rationale: An applicability scope is a structured key made of codes and references that is evaluated at resolution time; it has no document form, no rendition and no separate custody. Capturing it as an artifact would create a second identity for something that only exists as an attribute set on a preference statement.

findings.name: Preferred channel modality and relative preference ordering
findings.description: The party's positive disposition towards one or more channel kinds within a scope, expressed as a relative preference value that points at a channel kind or an endpoint handle owned by the channel area, never at an address. Includes the semantics of an absent preference value and whether values are comparable across different channel kinds.

answer_data: channel kind code
preference value on a stated scale
direction of the scale, lower or higher meaning more preferred

answer_data: default interpretation of absence
prohibition on absolute interpretation of a single value
comparison set definition

answer_data: comparison scope declaration

scale range and precision

questions.text: Which channel-kind or endpoint reference does the statement point to, and how is a reference that no longer resolves treated?
answer_data: endpoint handle or channel kind reference

data_elements.name: Channel kind
data_elements.description: Code for the modality a preference applies to, such as voice, text message, email, video or postal.

data_elements.name: Preference rank value
data_elements.description: Relative preference value within the declared comparison set, with the scale direction stated explicitly.

data_elements.name: Endpoint handle reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an endpoint descriptor held in the channel area; the address itself is never copied here.

data_elements.name: Preference comparison scope
data_elements.description: Declared set within which preference values may be compared, preventing cross-set numeric merging.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A modality preference is a small set of codes, references and one ordering value carried on the party record. It is consumed only by comparison at resolution time and has no standalone rendition, custody chain or media form that would justify artifact identity.

findings.name: Party-stated contact-avoidance preference
findings.description: An advisory request by the party to avoid a particular combination of channel, purpose, context or time. It is a local operational preference only: it carries no legal effect, is never evidence of a legal position, and can only ever narrow the set of options that other inputs already allow.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The statement is a narrow structured record plus an optional note, evaluated inline by the advisory resolver. Giving it artifact identity would invite treating it as a standalone, transferable instrument, which is precisely the confusion with an externally governed legal restriction record that this model must prevent.

layers.name: Linguistic and Accessibility Directives
layers.description: How a communication must be expressed to reach the party: language, script and locale preference, and functional accessibility accommodation directives that constrain which channels can satisfy the request.

It is resolved by comparison against channel capability at send time and produces no document, so an artifact would add identity and custody overhead with no corresponding content.

findings.name: Accessibility accommodation directive for contact
findings.description: Functional directives describing how communication must be conducted or rendered for this party, expressed as required channel capabilities and adaptation directives rather than as any diagnostic or medical statement, together with the required behaviour when no available channel can satisfy a directive.

questions.text: Which channel capabilities must a candidate option possess before the directive counts as satisfiable?
answer_data: required capability code such as textphone or relay support
capability source in the channel descriptor
satisfiability test outcome

questions.text: What must happen when no available channel can satisfy the accommodation directive?
answer_data: prescribed action such as flag and defer rather than silently degrade

questions.text: Which record is the authoritative source of this directive when an external accessibility profile also exists?
answer_data: reference to the external accessibility profile

data_elements.name: Accommodation directive
data_elements.description: Functional directive describing a required adaptation of the communication.

data_elements.name: Required channel capability
data_elements.description: Capability a candidate channel must expose for the directive to be satisfiable.

data_elements.name: Accommodation source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an external accessibility profile that is the authoritative source of the directive.

data_elements.name: Unsatisfiable directive action
data_elements.description: Declared behaviour when no candidate channel can satisfy the directive.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Accommodation directives are held as functional codes plus a reference to any authoritative external profile. Supporting documentation, assessments or accommodation letters are evidence objects owned by the accessibility or health model, so materialising an artifact here would pull evidence custody across a boundary this model does not own.

bundles.name: Availability and Routing
bundles.description: When the party asks to be contacted and in what order candidate options should be tried, including the time frame in which windows are read, urgency-driven deviation, and designation of a delegate or alternate recipient.
bundles.rationale: Availability and ordering form a coherent concern because they are all evaluated against an instant and a request, rather than being static assertions about the party. RFC 7953 treats stated availability as a priority-resolved pattern, FHIR carries rank as an ordering hint, and vCard registers agent and emergency relations - the same evaluation-time surface, grouped separately from static declaration and from precedence governance.

layers.name: Temporal Frame and Contact Windows
layers.description: The time-zone frame in which stated windows are interpreted, and the recurring or one-off intervals during which the party asks to be contacted or left alone.

findings.name: Time-zone reference and temporal frame
findings.description: The time zone in which the party's stated windows must be interpreted, preferring an IANA Time Zone Database identifier over a fixed UTC offset, together with the database release used and the distinction between a party's habitual zone and a per-statement override zone.

answer_data: pinned database release identifier

data_elements.name: Time-zone identifier

findings.inline_only_rationale: The temporal frame is one registry-governed identifier plus a release marker and a scope flag. The zone rules themselves live in the IANA registry, which this model references rather than reproduces, so there is nothing here to carry as a separate artifact.

findings.name: Stated contact windows and declared unavailability

layers.name: Ordering, Urgency and Delegation
layers.description: How candidate options are sequenced, when an urgency tier may deviate from stated windows, and who else may be contacted on the party's behalf.

findings.name: Attempt order and fallback sequence

Delivery outcomes and retry execution belong to the sending system.

bundles.name: Validity, Precedence and Statement Provenance
bundles.description: How long each statement holds, how temporary overrides supersede standing statements, how overlapping statements combine into one deterministic advisory outcome, and who asserted each statement under what authority.
bundles.rationale: Validity and precedence are a distinct concern from what a party declares and from when it is available: they govern how many independent statements plus one external input are folded into a single defensible outcome, and how that outcome can be explained later. RFC 7953 supplies a tested precedence pattern for overlapping availability, FHIR supplies validity periods, and JSCalendar supplies non-destructive override semantics.

layers.name: Effective Intervals, Overrides and Precedence
layers.description: The temporal validity of statements, non-destructive temporary overrides, and the deterministic precedence rules that combine local statements with the external restriction resolution status.

findings.name: Effective intervals and temporary overrides
findings.description: The validity interval bounding every preference statement, and the temporary override mechanism by which a short-lived statement supersedes a standing one for a bounded period without deleting or rewriting it.

questions.text: What effective interval bounds this statement, and what does an open-ended end mean?
answer_data: effective start instant
effective end instant or open marker
interpretation rule for an open end

questions.text: How does a temporary override supersede a standing statement without deleting it?
answer_data: supersedes reference from override to standing statement
override priority value
reinstatement behaviour at override expiry

questions.text: Is there a maximum permitted duration for a temporary override, and what happens at expiry?
answer_data: maximum override duration policy
expiry action such as automatic reinstatement
reconfirmation prompt where the override is repeatedly extended

questions.text: Which statement applies at an instant when several overrides are effective at once?
answer_data: priority ordering among overrides
equal-priority resolution rule favouring the more restrictive outcome
the identifier of the statement that governed the instant

answer_data: retention marker on the superseded version
adopting Dimension retention policy reference
minimum content kept after disposition

data_elements.name: Effective start
data_elements.description: Instant from which the statement applies.

data_elements.name: Effective end
data_elements.description: Instant after which the statement no longer applies; absence means open-ended.

data_elements.name: Temporary override flag
data_elements.description: Marks the statement as a bounded override of one or more standing statements.

data_elements.name: Override priority
data_elements.description: Priority value resolving overlap between simultaneously effective statements.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference from an override or new version to the statement version it supersedes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity intervals and supersession links are relational attributes on statement versions. They are meaningful only in place, as part of the statement graph the resolver walks, and extracting them into an artifact would create a parallel version history competing with the statement records themselves.

findings.name: Precedence and conflict-resolution rules
findings.description: The deterministic rules that fold matching statements, the local contact-avoidance preference and the external restriction resolution status into one advisory disposition per candidate option, including the fail-closed rule that an unresolvable external restriction reference yields an unresolved outcome rather than any permissive default.

questions.text: In which order are overlapping statements and external inputs combined into a single effective disposition?
answer_data: ordered precedence chain
per-step input and output disposition
the ruleset edition that defines the chain

questions.text: Which input may only narrow the result, and which input blocks an option outright?
answer_data: narrow-only inputs, including the local avoidance preference
blocking input, being the active external restriction
proof that no local input can re-permit a blocked option

questions.text: What must be returned when the external communication-restriction reference cannot be resolved at evaluation time?
answer_data: unresolved outcome value
reason code and retry guidance
explicit prohibition of a permissive default

questions.text: How is a genuine contradiction between two statements of equal precedence surfaced rather than silently resolved?
answer_data: conflict detection result with the conflicting statement identifiers
most-restrictive interim disposition
routing of the conflict to the responsible steward

questions.text: Which edition of the precedence ruleset produced a given resolution, and how is that recorded on the result?
answer_data: ruleset edition identifier
time-zone database release used
statement version identifiers cited by the result

data_elements.name: Precedence chain
data_elements.description: Ordered list of precedence steps applied when combining inputs into one disposition.

data_elements.name: External restriction reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the external communication-restriction registry entry applicable to this party, supplied by the governance area; carries binding and subject parameters only, never a copy of the restriction record.

data_elements.name: Restriction resolution status
data_elements.description: Outcome of resolving the external reference: an active restriction found, no restriction found, or not resolvable.

data_elements.name: Option disposition

data_elements.name: Precedence ruleset edition
data_elements.description: Identifier of the precedence ruleset edition that produced a resolution.

artifacts.name: Advisory precedence ruleset
artifacts.description: The published, versioned decision table that defines how matching statements, the local avoidance preference and the external restriction resolution status combine into one advisory disposition, including the fail-closed unresolved outcome. It is a declarative rule statement; running it, and enforcing any result, belong to the consuming system and to the external restriction registry respectively.
media_or_form: machine-readable rule set in the adopting projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Stable series identifier issued by the adopting Dimension plus a monotonically increasing edition number; every resolution result cites the exact edition, and superseded editions stay resolvable so a past outcome can be reconstructed.

layers.name: Statement Provenance and Assurance
layers.description: Who asserted each preference, under what authority, through which capture channel, and how statement time is separated from recording time.

findings.name: Provenance, authority and assurance of a preference statement
findings.description: The origin of each statement: the asserting party or authorised steward, the authority relied on, the capture channel and its assurance level, and the separate recording of the instant the party stated the preference and the instant the system recorded it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance here is a set of attributes carried on each statement version. The captured form itself, whether a signed web form submission, a call recording or a letter, is an evidence object whose custody, retention and audit trail belong to the capture and logging systems, so this model references it rather than materialising it.

functions.name: Declare or revise a preference statement
functions.description: Record a new preference, availability or routing statement for a party, or revise an existing one by supersession, with its scope, effective interval, asserter and authority.
inputs: Party reference resolvable in the parent party model
Applicability scope: purpose class, usage context and party capacity
Statement body: modality preference, avoidance request, language or accommodation directive, window pattern, ordering or delegation
Effective interval and any override marker
Asserter reference, asserter role and authority basis
Statement time supplied by the asserter
outputs: Persisted statement version with a local identifier, record time and supersession links
Validation report listing unresolved references, malformed codes and interval defects
preconditions: The party reference resolves in the parent party model
The asserter is authorised for the statement class being written
Referenced channel kinds and endpoint handles resolve in the channel area
Language tags, time-zone identifiers and purpose codes validate against their governing registries
The statement carries no assertion of legal effect
effects: Creates or supersedes a record inside this model's own statement set only
Links the new version to the version it supersedes rather than overwriting it
Sends no communication and schedules none
Creates, ends or modifies nothing in the external communication-restriction registry or the consent and legal-basis model

functions.name: Evaluate stated availability at an instant
functions.description: Determine whether an instant or interval falls inside the party's stated contact windows, after applying the time-zone frame, recurrence expansion, occurrence exceptions and effective overrides.
inputs: Statement set matching the applicable scope
Evaluation instant or interval as an RFC 3339 value with an explicit offset
Time-zone identifier and pinned time-zone database release
Effective temporary overrides at the evaluation instant
outputs: Window disposition: inside a stated window, outside a stated window, or no window declared
Identifier and version of the statement that governed the result
Applied time-zone identifier and database release
preconditions: The time-zone identifier resolves against the cited database release
The uncovered-time disposition is declared for the statement set
effects: Reads and writes nothing in the calendar system of record and asserts nothing about real free or busy time
Returns no-window-declared instead of assuming the party is contactable

functions.name: Resolve an advisory contact plan
functions.description: Produce an ordered advisory plan of candidate contact options for a request, by combining matching preference statements, stated availability, the local contact-avoidance preference and the resolution status of the external communication-restriction reference.
inputs: Party reference and request scope: purpose class, usage context and urgency tier
Evaluation instant as an RFC 3339 value with an explicit offset
Candidate options with channel kind and capability metadata supplied by the channel area
Resolvable external communication-restriction reference supplied by the governance area
Precedence ruleset edition identifier
outputs: Ordered advisory contact plan, or the single value unresolved
Per-option disposition with a reason code
Cited ruleset edition, time-zone database release and statement versions
preconditions: The external restriction reference is present; if it is absent or cannot be resolved, the function returns unresolved and produces no plan
Candidate options carry the capability metadata needed to test accommodation directives
A precedence ruleset edition is specified
effects: Any active external restriction blocks the applicable option and takes precedence over every local statement and every urgency tier
The local contact-avoidance preference may only remove options and can never permit what an external restriction prohibits
Returns unresolved rather than any permissive default when the restriction registry cannot be resolved
Produces advisory output only: it does not send, block, throttle, queue or log a communication, and it evaluates no legal basis
Writes nothing to the party record, the restriction registry or any delivery log

functions.name: Resolve language and rendering directives
functions.description: Select the language tag and rendering directives to use for a given candidate option, by matching the party's language preference and accommodation directives against the option's declared capabilities.
inputs: Ordered language preferences with context and modality qualifiers
Accommodation directives and their required channel capabilities
Declared capabilities of the selected candidate option
Content modality of the intended communication
outputs: Selected language tag in canonical form, with fallbacks in order
Rendering directives the sender must apply
Report of directives that the option cannot satisfy
preconditions: Language tags are well formed and canonicalised under BCP 47
The candidate option publishes a capability list
Script subtags have been tested against the Suppress-Script rule
effects: Produces advisory rendering directives only; it translates, transcribes and generates no content
Flags an unsatisfiable accommodation directive instead of silently degrading the communication
Discloses to a channel provider only the required capability, never the underlying need

functions.name: Explain a resolution outcome
functions.description: Render a human- and agent-readable explanation of how an advisory plan or an unresolved outcome was reached, naming the statements applied, narrowed, superseded or blocking.
inputs: A resolution result with its per-option dispositions
Precedence ruleset edition and the statement versions cited
Time-zone database release used
outputs: Ordered explanation of applied, narrowed, superseded and blocking inputs with reason codes
Explicit unresolved marker and its cause when no plan was produced
List of statement identifiers a steward should review where a contradiction was detected
preconditions: The resolution result cites statement versions and a ruleset edition
The requester is authorised to see the statement classes referenced
effects: Produces an explanation only; it changes no statement and re-runs no decision
Reports only the resolution status of the external restriction reference and never the content of the external restriction record
Is not an audit record and does not substitute for the sending or logging system's own trail, which those systems own and retain

composition.purpose: Attach preference, availability and routing statements to a governed party identity. Party identity, naming, roles and life events remain owned by the parent model and are referenced, never restated.

composition.target: Contact channel and endpoint descriptor area of WM-PER-010
composition.purpose: Preference statements bind to channel kinds and endpoint handles published by the channel area, which owns the endpoint address, its syntax, its capability metadata and its verification state. This area stores no address.

Carry only the resolvable reference and its resolution status as an input to the advisory resolver. The restriction record, its lifecycle, its evaluation and its enforcement stay with the registry; this model never creates, ends, weakens or interprets it, and returns unresolved when the reference cannot be resolved.
Point at the lawfulness decision without reproducing it. A stated preference is not consent evidence and a resolved plan is never a legal-basis determination.
Identify the consumer of an advisory plan. Delivery attempts, outcomes, retries and audit trails are created, owned and retained there; this model neither writes nor mirrors them.

composition.target: IETF JSContact (RFC 9553) and vCard (RFC 6350) preference vocabulary
composition.purpose: Map usage contexts, preference ordering, preferred languages, phone feature values and RELATED relation types. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed and the numeric comparison-scope rule of PREF is preserved rather than flattened.

Reuse recurring availability, occurrence override and priority-resolution semantics for stated contact windows, without adopting calendar scheduling, free/busy publication or scheduling-message workflows.
Use registry time-zone identifiers and pinned database releases to interpret stated local windows; the zone rules themselves are never copied into this model.

composition.target: BCP 47 / RFC 5646 language tag syntax and the IANA subtag registry
composition.purpose: Constrain language preference values to canonical BCP 47 tags, including the Suppress-Script rule for script subtags.

composition.target: 1EdTech / ISO-IEC 24751 AccessForAll Personal Needs and Preferences
composition.purpose: Express accommodation directives functionally and support multiple context-specific preference sets. The full functional-ability profile and any diagnostic content remain in the accessibility or health model.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR R5 ContactPoint (rank, period, use)
composition.purpose: Interoperate with health-sector exchange for preference ranking, validity periods and temporary use, noting that FHIR rank orders a set while vCard PREF is comparable only within one property.

Support publication of organisation-side contact purpose, available languages, available hours and accessibility options on the web, acknowledging that the published enumeration is far narrower than the functional directive set held here.

composition.target: OASIS Common Alerting Protocol v1.2 urgency vocabulary
composition.purpose: Offer a sector-neutral urgency tier vocabulary for escalation preference. CAP alert structure, dissemination and public-warning semantics are not adopted, and no CAP element grants override of an external restriction.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable steward per party profile; the default owner is the party, or an explicitly authorised identity steward acting under recorded authority.
The Dimension must register a resolvable external communication-restriction reference before enabling the advisory resolver; without it the resolver returns unresolved for every request.
The Dimension must pin and publish the time-zone database release, the precedence ruleset edition and the purpose-class code system its resolver uses.

The Dimension must declare its own retention, disposition and erasure policy for preference statements and for restricted free-text fields; this model sets no retention period and performs no erasure.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers are lower-kebab-case inside the model namespace and carry no date component. Externally governed values keep their source namespace and version: IANA vCard property and TYPE values, BCP 47 language tags, IANA time-zone identifiers, FHIR code system URIs and schema.org terms. Locally minted extensions use a registered vendor prefix following the IANA vCard registration procedure and are never minted into a registry namespace the Dimension does not control.
registry_links: IANA vCard Elements registries for properties, parameters and property values, including PREF, LANGUAGE, TEL types and RELATED types: https://www.iana.org/assignments/vcard-elements/vcard-elements.xhtml
IANA Time Zone Database for Area/Location identifiers and release pinning: https://www.iana.org/time-zones
BCP 47 language subtag syntax as defined by RFC 5646: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646.html

canonicalization_rules: Language tags are stored in BCP 47 canonical form with a script subtag only where it adds distinguishing value.
Time zones are stored as IANA Area/Location identifiers together with the database release used; a fixed offset is stored only as a flagged degraded fallback.
All time values are stored as RFC 3339 date-time strings with seconds precision and an explicit offset or Z.
Preference values are stored as integers on a declared scale together with the comparison scope in which they may be compared; values from different scopes are never merged into one ordering.
Statement sets are ordered deterministically by effective interval, then priority, then statement identifier, so that repeated resolution of the same inputs yields the same output.
patch_rules: A substantive change supersedes: a new statement version is written and linked to the version it replaces, which is retained.
Only a correction of a recording error patches a version in place, and it is marked as a correction with the correcting party and correction time.
A temporary override is written as its own bounded statement that supersedes for its interval; it never edits the standing statement.
A patch never alters, ends or annotates a record in the external communication-restriction registry or the consent and legal-basis model.
compatibility_rules: Adding a purpose class, channel capability or accommodation directive code is backward compatible; consumers must treat an unknown code as unknown, never as permission.

Narrowing the meaning of an existing code, inverting a preference scale direction, or changing the default disposition of uncovered time is breaking and requires a new major edition of the precedence ruleset.
A resolution result remains valid only while the cited ruleset edition, time-zone database release and statement versions are unchanged; otherwise it must be recomputed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact or statement, such as the availability system UID or the party master identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI from a normative registry or namespace, such as a vCard UID URI or a FHIR resource identifier.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension where no authoritative or governed identifier exists.
A date, a channel address, a display label or a preference value is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-time strings with seconds precision and an explicit numeric offset or Z. A local wall-clock window additionally carries an IANA time-zone identifier and the pinned database release, because an offset alone cannot express daylight-saving transitions. Event time, meaning the instant the party stated a preference or the instant a window starts, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the instant the statement was captured or loaded; when the two differ, both are mandatory, and a resolution result additionally records its own evaluation instant.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: A serial artifact such as the advisory precedence ruleset carries a stable series identifier plus a monotonically increasing edition number in the form series-id/vMAJOR.MINOR. The edition number, never a publication date, identifies the edition; every superseded edition stays resolvable so that a past resolution can be reconstructed.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest and the identifiers of the statement versions it was generated from. A cached resolution is valid only while its cited ruleset edition, time-zone database release and statement versions match; any digest or version mismatch invalidates the cache and forces re-resolution, and a failure to verify is treated as unresolved rather than as a usable result.

policies: Advisory-only policy: every output of this model is an input to someone else's sending decision. Blocking, throttling, sending, queuing and delivery logging are performed and owned by the consuming system and by the external restriction registry.

Monotonic narrowing policy: a local contact-avoidance preference may only remove options from a plan. It can never permit contact that an active external restriction prohibits, and no urgency tier changes this.

Fail-closed policy: an absent or unresolvable external communication-restriction reference yields the value unresolved. No permissive default is produced under any circumstance, including for high urgency tiers.

No-defaulting policy: life-safety routing, minority, vulnerability, workplace contact and region-specific marketing conditions are recorded explicitly as profile-conditional flags when they apply, and are never inferred, assumed or defaulted.

read: A read of preference statements requires a declared purpose recorded by the reading system; the response carries only the statement classes that purpose covers.
A read never resolves or discloses the content of the external communication-restriction record; only its resolution status, being active, none or unresolved, is exposed.
A resolution result is read together with the statement versions, ruleset edition and time-zone release that produced it, so the outcome can be re-derived.
create: A statement is created with its applicability scope, effective interval, asserter, asserter role, authority basis and statement time, plus the record time assigned on capture.
Creation validates every reference, covering party, channel handle, code system, time zone and language tag, before acceptance, and rejects a statement asserting legal effect.

Creating a local avoidance preference never creates or implies an entry in the external communication-restriction registry; a party asking for a legally binding restriction must be routed to that registry.
update: A substantive change writes a new statement version linked by a supersedes reference; the prior version is retained and stays resolvable.
A recording-error correction patches in place and is marked as a correction with the correcting party and correction time.
An update never rewrites history for the purpose of changing how a past resolution would be explained.
delete: Withdrawal of a preference statement is recorded as an end-dated, superseded version carrying a tombstone, holding statement identifier, scope key, effective interval and end reason, rather than a physical erase, so that a past advisory outcome remains explainable.

Retention periods and physical erasure for this model's own records are set and executed under the adopting Dimension's retention and disposition policy; this model defines no retention period and performs no erasure itself.
A tombstone retains only identifier, scope key, effective interval and end reason; restricted free text such as an avoidance reason note is removed at disposition rather than retained.

Deletion here never deletes, ends or weakens a record in the external communication-restriction registry, the consent and legal-basis model or any delivery log. Those models own their own deletion and its execution, and an erasure request touching them must be routed to them rather than satisfied locally.

roles.name: Party (preference subject)
responsibilities: State, revise and withdraw their own preferences, windows and avoidance requests
Designate or revoke a delegate or alternate contact
See which statements are recorded about them and how they were resolved

roles.name: Authorised identity steward
responsibilities: Record or amend preferences on the party's behalf only under recorded authority, with attribution
Route any request for a legally binding restriction to the external restriction registry rather than recording it locally
Resolve contradictions surfaced by the resolver with the party

roles.name: Dimension model steward
responsibilities: Maintain purpose-class, capability and urgency code systems and their versions
Publish precedence ruleset editions and pin the time-zone database release
Review that no bundle, finding or function has drifted into owning identity, delivery, consent or restriction semantics

roles.name: Consuming sender or agent
responsibilities: Supply purpose class, urgency tier and evaluation instant on every resolution request
Treat unresolved as non-permissive and honour the advisory plan and its reason codes
Own its own delivery attempts, outcomes and logging without writing them back into this model

roles.name: External restriction registry custodian
responsibilities: Own the legal restriction record, its lifecycle and its enforcement
Expose a resolvable reference and a resolution status to this model without exposing record content

access.default_rule: Least privilege by declared purpose: preference statements are readable only by roles with a recorded purpose for contacting the party, and only for the statement classes that purpose covers. Restricted free text, meaning avoidance reason notes, and accommodation directives are held at a higher restriction level than routing codes, because they can reveal sensitive characteristics.
exceptions: Life-safety routing statements may be read under a time-bounded break-glass grant when a declared life-safety purpose applies; the grant is issued and recorded by the granting system, not by this model.
An accommodation directive may be passed to a channel provider only as the minimal required capability, never as the underlying need or its free-text explanation.
A designated delegate may read the designation and the scope that applies to them, but not the party's unrelated statements.
An external restriction reference is readable as a status only; its record content is never exposed through this model at any scope.
audit_requirements: Every read of a restricted free-text field and every break-glass grant must be recorded by the system performing it; this model requires that such a record exist and be referenceable, while the audit trail itself is created, owned and retained by the adopting Dimension's logging model.

Every resolution result must cite the statement versions, precedence ruleset edition and time-zone database release used, so that a past outcome can be reconstructed from the statement set without depending on an audit log owned by this model.
Any operator amendment made on the party's behalf must carry the acting identity, the authority basis and both statement time and record time.

required_fields: Precedence ruleset edition and time-zone database release in force
read_order: AGENTS.md, for model name, type and the six bootstrap URLs, whatever the storage projection in use
Specification URL, for the scope statement, out-of-scope list and boundary notes, read before any write or resolution
Processes URL, for the declare, evaluate, resolve and explain functions with their preconditions and effects
Storage type URL and Interface URL, for the projection actually in use, whether JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP or MongoDB, which carries no semantics of its own
External communication-restriction reference resolution URL, confirmed reachable before the advisory resolver is enabled; if it is not, every resolution returns unresolved

coverage.claim: This result covers only the communication-preference, routing and availability area of WM-PER-010 as assigned by the split-pass brief: applicability scope, preferred and avoided modalities, language and accessibility directives, time-zone frame and stated contact windows, attempt ordering, urgency and delegation, effective intervals and overrides, precedence rules and statement provenance. The model block states the boundary of the combined WM-PER-010, whose channel and governance areas are delivered separately. Structure is grounded in IETF vCard, JSContact, Calendar Availability, JSCalendar and BCP 47, HL7 FHIR R5 ContactPoint, IANA registries, schema.org and the 1EdTech/ISO-IEC 24751 AccessForAll model. Constructs without primary support are marked as gaps rather than presented as canonical.

checklist.notes: Artifact identity priority leads with the authoritative master-system identifier, then a governed IRI, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID; dates, addresses and preference values are explicitly excluded as identifiers. Party and delegate identity are referenced into WM-PER-001, not restated.

Effective intervals, non-destructive supersession, temporary overrides with expiry and delegation lapse are modelled. Lifecycle of the external restriction record and of delivery events is explicitly left with those models.

Statements bind to channel handles, party capacities, delegates and superseded versions by reference. Thirteen composition links separate owned structure from aligned standards and referenced governed objects.

IANA time-zone identifiers with pinned releases, recurring windows with occurrence overrides, RFC 3339 values with seconds and explicit offsets, and separate statement and record times. Uncovered-time disposition is declared rather than assumed.
Asserter, asserter role, authority basis, capture channel and assurance level are carried per statement version, and every resolution cites ruleset edition, time-zone release and statement versions.
The party owns their preferences; a steward may act only under recorded authority. Five roles delimit who may write, resolve and consume, and the restriction registry custodian is named as external.

Reference resolution, code-system validation, BCP 47 canonicalisation, satisfiability testing of accommodation directives against channel capability, and explicit surfacing of irreducible contradictions rather than silent resolution.

Purpose-scoped least privilege across bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes, with break-glass, minimal-capability disclosure and delegate-scoped exceptions. Audit execution is required but owned by the Dimension's logging model.

Withdrawal produces an end-dated tombstone with restricted free text removed at disposition. Retention periods and physical erasure are executed under the adopting Dimension's policy, and deletion never touches the external restriction, consent or delivery models.

Alignments to vCard/JSContact, FHIR R5, schema.org, RFC 7953 and RFC 8984, BCP 47, IANA tzdb and AccessForAll are declared as alignments only, with five recorded conflicts including the PREF versus rank comparison-scope trap.

Functional accommodation directives with required channel capabilities and a mandatory unsatisfiable-directive action, grounded in AccessForAll and the textphone and relay capability values registered by IANA and schema.org.
BCP 47 tags with modality, context and order, the Suppress-Script omission rule, declared fallbacks, and an explicit boundary excluding number and date formatting conventions.
A published, versioned precedence ruleset with monotonic narrowing, external-restriction supremacy and a fail-closed unresolved outcome, patterned on RFC 7953 priority resolution.

No primary, sector-neutral standard defines urgency tiers for party contact preference. CAP v1.2 supplies an alert-oriented vocabulary used strictly as an alignment candidate, so the tier set is a designed construct requiring Dimension-level definition.

vCard, JSContact, FHIR and schema.org define no advisory, non-legal contact-avoidance construct distinct from a legally governed restriction. The finding is a designed construct, defensible from the absence of coverage in those standards but not directly attested by any of them.

Party-side preference needs only a time-zone frame; geographic service area exists in schema.org for organisation contact points but belongs to the channel or organisation model, not to a party's preference statement.
Transport security, authentication of the requesting system and key management belong to the interface and platform layers, which are projections outside this format-neutral model.

known_omissions: Frequency capping and quiet-hour enforcement across a whole programme are not modelled; only the party's stated spacing preference is carried, and enforcement is external.
Organisation-side routing rotas, on-call schedules and queue assignment are not modelled; this area covers a party's stated preference, not a service desk's staffing.
Inbound contact handling, meaning how the party's own inbound requests are queued or triaged, is not modelled beyond stated windows.
Verification of a delegate's identity or mandate is referenced but not modelled; the authority record lives elsewhere.
No mapping table is provided from purpose classes to jurisdiction-specific marketing or solicitation categories, which would import a regional rule into a neutral schema.
Cost, carrier economics and channel reliability metrics that a sender might weigh alongside preference are out of scope.
The channel and endpoint area and the governance area of the combined WM-PER-010 are delivered by other split passes and are only referenced here.
conflicts: vCard and JSContact define pref as interpretable only relative to other instances of the same property in the same card, while FHIR ContactPoint.rank orders a set of contact points. A naive round trip between them silently changes the comparison scope, so this model records the comparison scope explicitly.

RFC 7953 defaults time inside a VAVAILABILITY that no AVAILABLE component covers to busy, whereas schema.org hoursAvailable publishes open hours with no normative default for uncovered time. The two conventions imply opposite defaults, so the uncovered-time disposition is a required declared element here.

RFC 7953 PRIORITY treats 1 as highest with absence or 0 as lowest, while vCard PREF treats 1 as most preferred with absence as least preferred. Both invert ordinary intuition in different ways and must never be merged into a single numeric field.

schema.org ContactPointOption offers only TollFree and HearingImpairedSupported, far narrower than functional AccessForAll directives; mapping from directives to that enumeration is lossy in one direction and must not be reversed.

The 1EdTech AccessForAll PNP v2.0 information model expresses language preference with ISO 639-2 codes, while vCard, JSContact and schema.org require BCP 47. Codes must be converted with an explicit mapping, never copied across.
regional_assumptions: Marketing and solicitation rules, statutory quiet hours and emergency-number routing are jurisdiction-specific. They are treated as profile-conditional inputs resolved by the external restriction registry and are deliberately not encoded as schema invariants.
The window model assumes the Gregorian calendar and IANA time-zone identifiers; expressing windows in alternative calendar systems is not modelled.

A single authoritative external communication-restriction registry per Dimension is assumed. A party subject to several jurisdictions may resolve to more than one, and aggregation across multiple registries is undefined in this area and must be settled by the governance area.
Rules for contacting minors, vulnerable persons and people at their workplace vary by jurisdiction and sector, so they are recorded as explicit flags rather than as behaviour built into the resolver.
Relay and textphone service availability, and the accessibility obligations attached to them, differ by country; capability codes are carried, but no obligation is asserted.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to make the resolver produce a usable plan when the external restriction reference is unreachable. Rejected: unresolved is the only outcome, it is stated in the function effects, in the fail-closed policy and in the integrity rule, and no bundle, layer, finding or function contains a permissive fallback.

Attempted to model the legally governed restriction locally under a preference-sounding name. Rejected: only a resolvable reference and a resolution status are carried, the record content is never exposed at any access scope, and creation, deletion and patch rules all forbid touching the external registry.

Attempted to attach delivery outcomes, retry state, bounce handling and audit trails to the attempt-order finding. Rejected: attempt ordering is a stated preference and the fallback trigger is explicitly evaluated by the sending system, which owns its own logs; the explain function is stated not to be an audit record.

Tested whether a high urgency tier could override an active external restriction. Rejected: urgency may override only the party's own windows and avoidance statements, and the constraint question, the override-allowance element and the resolver effects all state that the external restriction takes precedence.

Checked whether an endpoint address, party name or message content leaked into any finding or data element. None do: every such value is carried as a reference to the channel area, the party model or the message model.

Checked whether accessibility directives could imply a diagnosis. They are expressed functionally per AccessForAll, a dedicated privacy question forbids diagnostic vocabulary, and disclosure to a channel provider is limited to the required capability.

Searched vCard, JSContact, FHIR R5 and schema.org for a primary definition of an advisory, non-legal contact-avoidance preference and of party-contact urgency tiers. Neither exists; both are recorded as coverage gaps and as designed constructs rather than presented as canonical.

Compared every bundle, layer, finding and function against the composition ledger. The known-relation ledger supplied for this model is empty, so the check was run against the registry parent WM-PER-001 and against every link declared here; target-owned concepts, namely party identity, endpoint address, calendar free/busy, consent evidence, restriction lifecycle and enforcement, delivery events and audit trails, were moved to composition links, out_of_scope entries or boundary notes and are modelled nowhere locally.
